task_specification.objective: Restore a closure-ready ordinary five-wave run with a truthful, accessible upgrade decision surface; repair authored cemetery spatial visibility and collision through explicit binding/isolation; and keep dense profiling recapture-ready without falsely qualifying software rendering.

diagnosis.root_cause: Release convergence has two distinct causes: the cemetery camera still classifies the gameplay MausoleumCollision footprint as a sightline occluder despite the intended layer split, so landmark coverage reports zero visibility; dense qualification is blocked by the external llvmpipe renderer gate rather than a proven candidate performance defect. The ordinary route and upgrade transaction need one closure-ready, non-diagnostic replay.

stop_conditions: Do not claim native dense qualification, a performance pass, or three-cycle acceptance while the host renderer remains llvmpipe/software.
Do not replace, split, duplicate, hide, or surgically modify the intact authored cemetery package; stop if spatial integrity cannot be proven without that package.
Do not accept a diagnostic wave jump, a placeholder upgrade value, or a static landmark screenshot as ordinary release evidence.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different strategy from prior camera transform tuning: restore the authored collider-to-visual binding and explicitly isolate camera sight queries from gameplay collision while retaining movement collision; make the ordinary route and upgrade transaction directly replayable; and harden only the dense receipt/handoff contract, carrying the renderer limitation forward for host-native recapture.

code: Run bounded Godot parse/import checks for every changed GDScript, scene, and resource; confirm no runtime error spam, invalid freed-instance access, NaN movement, or duplicate terminal transitions.

Exercise white-box snapshots for ordinary_route_wave_ids, route_contiguous, boss_requested_exactly_once, upgrade_transaction_receipt, authoritative selection/application, spatial collision alignment, camera occluder bindings, and dense preflight/cycle receipts.
runtime: Task ordinary_route_and_upgrade_transaction: from a fresh title Play, use ordinary movement and automatic combat through all five waves; capture each wave transition, wave-3 elite, Bellkeeper telegraph/phase/recovery/defeat, one natural XP overflow draft, selected-upgrade combat response, victory/result, and clean Retry.

Task authored_cemetery_spatial_integrity: capture before/near/after landmark frames, four cardinal first-person native-street views, perimeter traversal, landmark-side collision probes, spawn/exclusion checks, mouse horizontal and vertical probes, and camera/HUD input ownership receipts.

Task dense_profile_native_handoff: on the matching native hardware renderer at 1920x1080, run three serial dense prepare→advance→reset cycles at 25-40 enemies and retain software-rejected evidence separately; compare lifecycle and high-water marks across retries.
visual: Compare ordinary and dense shipped-camera captures against the bound Mournlight reference for high-angle playable framing, cemetery density, warm lantern versus cool moonlight, readable silhouettes, escape lanes, and compact HUD.

Inspect the level-up page at the PRD reference resolution and supported UI scales for icon/silhouette-first hierarchy, no more than three truthful deltas, no NEW/LOCKED CURRENT placeholders, and complete mouse/keyboard/gamepad focus states.

Inspect landmark and perimeter views for grounded collision alignment, no landmark disappearance/occlusion drift, coherent external depth on all edges, no visible primitive stand-ins, and no empty-edge void.

done_when: A fresh ordinary run advances contiguously through wave IDs first_toll, crossing_shadows, gravewind, long_procession, and bellkeeper without tester jumps or diagnostic qualification, with intermissions and upgrade pauses owned by the authoritative run controller.

Wave composition visibly escalates: Wispbat flank pressure appears in wave 2, a ranged lane and Grave Brute elite appear in wave 3, mixed representative density with a recoverable escape lane appears in wave 4, and the Bellkeeper wave has controlled supporting pressure.

The Bellkeeper has a readable warning, bell-wave telegraph, alternating lane-pressure or summon behavior, two authoritative phases, a vulnerable recovery window, exactly-once defeat, victory transition, and no spawning after victory or failure.

Enemy wisps preserve XP overflow, exactly one paused draft opens per threshold, gameplay clocks and enemy motion remain paused during the draft, held confirm cannot double-apply, and the selected upgrade mutates authoritative build state before the next combat event resumes.

The choice hierarchy is a visual hierarchy: lead each option with weapon or upgrade silhouettes or icons, show truthful current-to-new values, show no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, omit unchanged or placeholder CURRENT values including NEW/LOCKED, and provide keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states without clipping at the reference viewport.

The next relevant attack or utility event visibly reflects the selected upgrade, and focused runs can retain the three distinct build identities: focused bolts, close sweeps, and orbiting area control.
tasks.instructions: Own the ordinary release route and its decision transaction across the run controller, wave director, wave resource, Bellkeeper, upgrade draft controller/view, and upgrade catalog. Replace any evidence-only or diagnostic route dependency with real elapsed-time progression and pause-safe intermissions; keep terminal ownership single-shot and stop spawns after terminal state. Audit the existing authored card hierarchy in the real upgrade-draft scene/controller rather than adding a text form. The choice hierarchy must be a visual hierarchy with silhouettes or icons, truthful current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, and keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus. Retain debounced selection, explicit unavailable states, and complete mouse/keyboard/gamepad focus behavior. Make the transaction state and applied modifier observable in runtime snapshots for black-box and white-box retest. Preserve the three weapon identities and make the normal route usable for distinct successful build-shape runs.

done_when: Make a real expand change or otherwise bind a larger traversable scale from the intact authored package; report before/after playable extents and time-to-cross rather than asserting the existing rectangle is sufficient.

The shipped camera shows an actual external world or external depth beyond every playable perimeter edge using spatial dressing, not only fog, sky, exposure, or a color change; the authored package remains one intact runtime instance.

The central building/landmark collider is bound in the same transform space as its rendered footprint, and ordinary movement or movement replay around every side cannot pass through it, become hidden inside it, or cause disappearance/occlusion of a still-relevant landmark.

Keeper post, mausoleum, and cracked bell remain visible and readable before approach, at near contact, and after departure; camera handling uses bounded selective transparency or sight-lane isolation and never hard-hides the whole landmark.

The boundary/perimeter remains grounded and aligned with visible geometry, preserves a coherent loop and cross-route, leaves at least one recoverable escape lane, and keeps spawn exclusion and navigation on the native streets.

done_when: The candidate-side dense collector records renderer classification, hardware eligibility, viewport, frame execution, nonzero frame/physics samples, requested/resolved density, subsystem samples, high-water marks, lifecycle deltas, reset isolation, and cycle identity for each of three cycles.

The collector remains editor-only and release-safe; it never suppresses real sampling merely because the renderer is software, but reports rejected_software_renderer for llvmpipe and leaves native qualification pending rather than fabricating a pass.

Three serial prepare, advance, and reset receipts preserve setup_generation, advance_generation, requested/resolved, cycle_id, and next-frame reset isolation with no stale actors, duplicated callbacks, or unbounded live-node, audio, memory, or input growth in the receipt.

The source contract remains aligned to the 1920x1080, 25-40 ordinary-enemy profile with all weapon families, pickups, animation, VFX, lights, UI, audio, and three retries; any missing field is repaired without changing ordinary gameplay balance.
